def unique_digits(x):
    
    odd_digit_elements = []
    for i in x:
        if all (int(c) % 2 == 1 for c in str(i)):
            odd_digit_elements.append(i)
    return sorted(odd_digit_elements)

def test_unique_digits():
    # Basic case: mixed numbers, only all-odd-digit numbers kept, result sorted
    assert unique_digits([15, 33, 1422, 1]) == [1, 15, 33]

    # No elements with all odd digits
    assert unique_digits([152, 323, 1422, 10]) == []

    # Empty input list
    assert unique_digits([]) == []

    # All even digits -> empty result
    assert unique_digits([2, 4, 6, 222]) == []

    # Single odd digits
    assert unique_digits([1, 3, 5, 7, 9]) == [1, 3, 5, 7, 9]

    # Multi-digit odd numbers, verify sorting of unsorted input
    assert unique_digits([979, 135, 3, 11]) == [3, 11, 135, 979]

    # Zero contains an even digit -> excluded
    assert unique_digits([0]) == []

    # Numbers containing 0 as a digit are excluded
    assert unique_digits([101, 303, 13]) == [13]

    # Duplicates are preserved (function does not deduplicate)
    assert unique_digits([1, 1, 3, 3]) == [1, 1, 3, 3]

    # Sorting check with varied lengths
    assert unique_digits([333, 1, 57, 9]) == [1, 9, 57, 333]

    # Large numbers with all odd digits
    assert unique_digits([111111, 2468, 97531]) == [111111, 97531]

    # Negative numbers raise ValueError ('-' cannot be converted to int)
    try:
        unique_digits([-13])
        assert False, "Expected ValueError for negative input"
    except ValueError:
        pass


if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_unique_digits()
    print("All tests passed!")

def test_unique_digits():
    # Basic case: mixed odd and even digit numbers
    assert unique_digits([15, 33, 1422, 1]) == [1, 15, 33]

    # All numbers contain even digits except one
    assert unique_digits([152, 3231, 103, 555]) == [555]

    # Empty input list
    assert unique_digits([]) == []

    # No elements have all odd digits
    assert unique_digits([2, 4, 6, 20, 84]) == []

    # All elements have odd digits, already sorted
    assert unique_digits([11, 13, 15, 17]) == [11, 13, 15, 17]

    # Single element with odd digits
    assert unique_digits([1]) == [1]

    # Single element with an even digit
    assert unique_digits([12]) == []

    # Duplicates are preserved
    assert unique_digits([15, 15, 1]) == [1, 15, 15]

    # Result is sorted regardless of input order
    assert unique_digits([331, 15, 1]) == [1, 15, 331]

    # Multi-digit numbers with all odd digits
    assert unique_digits([135, 246, 579, 8, 97531]) == [135, 579, 97531]

    # Large numbers
    assert unique_digits([111111, 222222, 999999]) == [111111, 999999]

    # Unsorted input with mixed values
    assert unique_digits([999, 888, 777, 666]) == [777, 999]

def test_unique_digits():
    # Basic mixed case: only elements with all odd digits are kept, sorted
    assert unique_digits([15, 33, 1422, 1]) == [1, 15, 33]

    # No elements with all odd digits
    assert unique_digits([152, 323, 1422, 10]) == []

    # Empty input list
    assert unique_digits([]) == []

    # Single element with odd digits
    assert unique_digits([1]) == [1]

    # All elements have odd digits, verify sorted order
    assert unique_digits([111, 11, 1111]) == [11, 111, 1111]

    # All elements contain even digits
    assert unique_digits([2, 4, 6, 8]) == []

    # Multi-digit odd-digit numbers sorted ascending
    assert unique_digits([135, 79, 357, 9]) == [9, 79, 135, 357]

    # Already sorted input stays sorted
    assert unique_digits([13, 15, 17, 19]) == [13, 15, 17, 19]

    # Zero is an even digit, so excluded
    assert unique_digits([0, 2, 20]) == []

    # Repeated odd digits across multiple elements
    assert unique_digits([999, 111, 333]) == [111, 333, 999]

    # Large numbers with all odd digits
    assert unique_digits([13579, 97531, 11111]) == [11111, 13579, 97531]

    # Mixed single and multi-digit results
    assert unique_digits([3, 12, 35, 44, 57]) == [3, 35, 57]
